contract: offline artifact / fault-injection corpus (fix-dv-19.01) — each case injects a fault, runs a state/output ORACLE (not a protocol/provider stub judging itself), and records exit/trace/environment. The DV-19 rule: the original COUNTEREXAMPLE must FAIL on the pre-fix behaviour and PASS after the fix; a positive is verified by STATE and OUTPUTS, tied to the release the fix shipped in. Judged by test/audit_regressions/fix-dv-19.01.py, stdlib only.
release_tie: the fix ships in a tagged release; a counterexample that passes pre-fix is not a fix

environment.note: provider/protocol stubs are inputs, never the oracle

cases.fault: SIGKILL between the processed_event marker INSERT and the business effect
cases.prefix_expect: FAIL (event eaten: marker present, effect never applied)
cases.postfix_expect: PASS (marker+effect one transaction/outbox → effect applied once)

cases.fault: February→January: a shorter period arrives after a longer one
cases.postfix_expect: PASS (both periods granted; reconciliation carries event.id)

cases.fault: two concurrent refunds (4000 then 9000) both read the same stored total
cases.prefix_expect: FAIL (9000 blind-writes over 4000-based total; a rollback clobbers newer)
cases.postfix_expect: PASS (CAS/re-read under lock; the loser re-reads, newer total wins)
